draft.title: Islamic ethics
card: Sharia means the path or way set out by God. It guides how Muslims live, in worship, family life, business and conduct towards others.
Sharia is drawn mainly from the Quran and the Hadith. Muslim scholars also study these sources to work out guidance on new questions.
Actions are judged as permitted (halal) or forbidden (haram). Some acts fall between these, such as those that are discouraged but not forbidden.
Muslims see ethical living as obedience to God. A person's choices are guided by what God has revealed, not only by personal opinion.
draft.remember: Sharia draws on the Quran and Hadith to guide Muslims in judging actions as permitted or forbidden.

a.q: What is the main purpose of Sharia for Muslims?
opts: To guide how they live by what God has revealed
To record the history of the early Muslim community
To list the five daily prayer times for each region
To replace the Quran with rules made by scholars
a.why: Sharia is the path set out by God, and it guides daily life and ethical choices. It does not replace the Quran, because it is drawn from the Quran and Hadith.
a.clue: Think about what the word Sharia means: a path.

b.q: Amira is a Muslim in Perth. She is unsure whether a new business deal is allowed. Which approach fits Islamic ethics?
opts: Check the Quran and Hadith, or ask a scholar who uses them
Decide by what most of her friends feel is fair
Choose whatever gives her the greatest profit
Wait until a government law covers the deal
b.why: Sharia is drawn from the Quran and Hadith, and scholars study these sources to guide new questions. Following friends or profit alone is wrong because ethical choices are judged by what God has revealed.
b.clue: Which sources is Sharia drawn from?

a.best: To guide how they live by what God has revealed

b.best: Check the Quran and Hadith, or ask a scholar who uses them
